findings.description: SonarQube is not configured for this project (no sonar-project.properties or .sonarqube.properties found). TD-85 requires all AI-generated code to pass static code analysis before merge.
findings.suggestion: Configure SonarQube for the project and run a scan on the changed branch, then re-review. This is a governance gate and is independent of the code quality of the change itself, which is sound (see notes below).

findings.description: TearDown() calls calc.reset(), which is redundant: the std::unique_ptr member is destroyed automatically when the fixture instance is torn down, releasing the Calculator. It is not a defect.
findings.suggestion: Optional. The explicit reset() can be kept intentionally as it makes the SetUp/TearDown symmetry visible, which is pedagogically useful for an educational unit-testing chapter. No change required.

findings.description: Calculator is a trivial value type, so a plain 'Calculator calc;' fixture member would suffice; the std::unique_ptr adds heap allocation not required by the type itself. However, using make_unique in SetUp and reset in TearDown is a reasonable way to demonstrate explicit per-test construction/destruction lifecycle for teaching purposes.
findings.suggestion: No change required. If maximum simplicity is preferred over demonstrating pointer lifecycle, a value member initialized in SetUp would be equivalent and null-safe by construction.

code_review_notes.googletest_fixture_usage: Correct. CalculatorTest_02 derives from testing::Test; SetUp()/TearDown() use valid 'override' signatures; TEST_F references a valid fixture type. All eight TEST_F cases access the fixture member via calc-> as intended.
code_review_notes.cpp_lifetime_and_null_safety: Safe. calc is a fixture-owned std::unique_ptr constructed in SetUp(), which GoogleTest guarantees to run before each test body, so every calc-> dereference is non-null. Ownership is unique; there is no leak, double-free, or dangling reference. TearDown()/automatic destruction release the object between tests, giving isolated per-test state.
code_review_notes.behavior_equivalence: Preserved. Inputs and assertions are identical to the original TEST-based cases and to unit_test_01.cpp (add/sub/mul/div happy and negative paths). Only the object-provisioning mechanism changed from a local Calculator to a fixture member.
code_review_notes.educational_clarity: Good. The change cleanly illustrates the SetUp/TearDown lifecycle contrasted with unit_test_01.cpp's per-test local instances.

residual_risks: Governance/process risk (blocking): no static-analysis (SonarQube) evidence exists for the change per TD-85. Once SonarQube is configured and passes, the change is expected to be mergeable.

The root CTest does not discover tests directly; regression evidence relies on the focused chapter CTest (16/16 GoogleTest cases pass) plus POST_BUILD hooks. Low technical risk given the change is confined to one test file.
No functional/correctness/security risk identified in the code change itself.
summary: Code change is technically correct, lifetime/null-safe, behavior-equivalent, and educationally clear; verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES solely because SonarQube static analysis is not configured (TD-85 governance gate).
